children: US and China Take Different AI Paths
China has established regulations covering areas such as AI algorithms and training data, including requirements for clearly labeling AI-generated content.
The U.S. under Trump has taken a less prescriptive approach, with the president arguing against imposing new AI-specific regulations.

Trump said at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that he rejected efforts to create a global framework to control AI. He described the technology as amazing while indicating that the U.S. would approach its development carefully.
The president also stated that the Justice Department could intervene if AI companies cause serious problems, while rejecting regulations he says could stifle U.S. innovation.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll released Tuesday showed broad concern among U.S. adults over AI safety, with 73% saying companies are not doing enough to prevent catastrophic outcomes.
